identity.title: TRAP complex is essential for coronavirus replication and glycoprotein biogeneses.

content.abstract: Coronaviruses remodel the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) to build replication organelles while producing heavily glycosylated membrane proteins, but the mechanisms coordinating these demands are unclear. Here, we describe the ER-resident translocon-associated protein (TRAP/SSR) complex as a conserved host dependency across diverse coronaviruses. Using porcine hemagglutinating encephalomyelitis virus (PHEV) as a model, we identify TRAPgamma in a genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screen as essential for productive viral infection. TRAPgamma depletion suppresses viral replication, disrupts canonical replication organelle formation, and amplifies innate immune signaling. Viral glycoproteins (nsp4, Spike, and hemagglutinin-esterase) selectively engage specific TRAP subunits (alpha, beta, gamma, and delta), and reducing their signal-sequence hydrophobicity compromises glycoprotein production and N-glycosylation, consistent with impaired co-translational ER targeting or translocation. Inhibition of the oligosaccharyltransferase (OST) complex recapitulates these defects, supporting a sequential signal recognition particle (SRP)-TRAP-OST axis. Thus, our findings reveal an essential role for the TRAP complex in viral subversion of ER proteostasis, highlighting ER co‑translational translocation machinery as a pivotal host-pathogen interface during the viral lifecycle.
